correctness.rationale: For J>0 and strictly positive local rates, the dark complement of the detector Krylov space is invariant and annihilated by the loss. An eigenvector of the graph evolution's effective Hamiltonian with a real eigenvalue must have zero amplitude at each detector by its loss expectation, so the bright restriction has strictly negative imaginary spectrum and decays even with Jordan blocks. The remaining trace is exactly the dark projector weight for any density matrix. The radial block eigenvalues are 1±√(1+na²), and the rim Fourier eigenvalues are c_k with pairs of multiplicity two except the even alternating endpoint. Counting multiples of n/gcd(n,2d) strictly below n/2 gives the displayed baseline. The two independent point evaluations on a merged radial/Fourier eigenspace have one row proportional to the other only at phase +1, while the total separated rank is already two at phase −1: the rank drops by one exactly outside the −1 case, including at the one-column endpoint. If there was no generic dark mode at even n=2s, then gcd(s,d)=1; phase −1 would force s|k, ruling it out at an interior collision. Odd n cannot have phase −1, and d=1 at the even endpoint works. The hub detector separates the radial vector at a collision, leaving one rim direction per distinct Fourier frequency plus two radial directions. The independently constructed algebraic Krylov ranks (python3 /workspace/review_evidence/reproduce.py 3) confirm generic, tuned and detuned cases, irrational squared tunings and all distances for the selected sizes. These finite checks are not the all-size proof.

The 0 radial Laplacian eigenvalue is isolated just as λ_+ is. Match corresponding radial eigenvectors normalized to have rim entries 1, mapping the positive adjacency radial vector to (1,...,1,1) and the negative one to (1,...,1,−n); extend this invertible map by the identity on the rim zero-sum sector. It preserves all rim evaluations since all four radial eigenvectors have the same normalized rim entries. It therefore maps each adjacency eigenspace (including each merged one) onto the matching Laplacian eigenspace and identifies their rim-detector kernels. The exact Laplacian rank law pulls back on the whole positive a-domain (g>2/n). This is a reduction of the dimension and placement laws, not an equality of all time evolutions or orthogonal projectors.
